ops.title: No switches: every test runs, always — no env gates, no opt-in coverage, no defensive guards
ops.body:
Directive from yasyf, 2026-08-02, following the test-fake sweep.

"We dont want any extra switches, env vars, options, or unnecessary defensiveness."

This is the testing counterpart of STYLEGUIDE §1 (fail fast, no fallbacks, no guards against
impossible states). Coverage that only runs when someone remembers a variable is coverage that does
not run. Three separate defects this phase were invisible to the default suite because the thing
that would have caught them was either faked or gated off.

## To remove

- **DAEMONKIT_E2E_LAUNCHD** — e2e_launchd_test.go:41 and deploy/e2e_launchd_test.go:37. The
  real-launchd end-to-end suite skips entirely without it. It is the suite that found ExitTimeOut
  firing at ~6s, ThrottleInterval dominating restarts, and that nothing but SIGKILL unparks a parked
  daemon — none of which the default suite can see. It runs always.
- **DAEMONKIT_TRUST_E2E** — internal/trust/verify_signed_test.go:20. Gates the signed-peer trust
  E2E and additionally requires .trust-fixtures built by hand via scripts/trust-fixtures.sh.
  Fixture construction becomes part of the normal test setup, not a manual prerequisite. This
  closes the standing task "G4: give the signed-peer E2E a CI home" — the answer is that it has no
  separate home, it is simply in the suite.

## What this costs, stated up front

Every test run bootstraps and boots out real LaunchAgents in the developer session and signs real
fixtures. It is slower and it mutates real machine state. That is the trade being taken
deliberately: a suite that is honest and slow beats one that is fast because it asks nothing real.

## Not switches — do not remove these

DAEMONKIT_SPAWNED_NONCE and DAEMONKIT_SPAWNED_LIMITS are the production ChannelHandoff conveyance.
DAEMONKIT_HOME and DAEMONKIT_AGENT_OWNER are production. The *_CHILD_*, *_TEST_CHILD_ROLE, and
FILE_LOCK_*_TEST_* variables are how a self-execd child selects its TestMain branch — that is the
mechanism the fork-bomb harness depends on, not a user-facing option.

## Also in scope: conditional skips

A t.Skip that fires on the machines state is the same defect in another shape. Present:
- internal/proc/inventory_test.go:389,449 and executable_test.go:122 — skip when no process owned
  by another user exists.
- internal/state/state_test.go:320, durable/fs_test.go:35 — skip when running as root.
- internal/trust/limitation_test.go:113 — skip when csops_audittoken is unavailable.
- own_test.go:671,1325 — skip when the case the test exists to exercise did not arise ("the ladder
  proved the exit inside a spent budget", "every one of N concurrent Adopts landed inside its
  budget"). These report as passes while asserting nothing.

Each needs either a real setup that guarantees the precondition, or deletion. A test that cannot
guarantee its own precondition is not a test.

Legitimate: internal/trust/limitation_test.go:252 documents a limitation (TF5 fd delegation needs a
privileged multi-process harness) and flock_test.go:165,238 are child-only helper entry points
driven by their parent test — those are dispatch, not conditional coverage.
ops.when: Before adding any env var, flag, build tag, t.Skip, or conditional guard to daemonkit — and when finishing the de-fake sweep
